Judge library extraction (judges.ts, 1162 LOC, 10 reusable factories) eliminated 120+ lines of duplicate DB query code per scenario. Each factory is simple, well-named, composable. Pattern successful for rule-based evaluation.

Seeding library extension (8 new helpers: seedThread, seedItem, seedRoutine, seedUserSkill, etc.) enables rich scenario composition. All 24 feature scenarios use library exclusively; no direct db.insert() calls. Seeding pattern is stable and reusable.

Type safety maintained across 12,727 LOC. All files pass `npm run check` strict mode. No unsafe casts. Return types explicit. TypeScript caught module-level state pattern risks early (A1 finding at code-review time, not production).

Per-feature scenario coverage complete: all 24 interactions have scenarios. Distribution: 9 features with 3-4 scenarios each (tool interactions), 9 systemic/compound features with 3-8 scenarios. Diversity analysis correctly determined counts.

Module-level `let` variables (40 instances across 11 files) couple seed()→judges via file-level state mutation. Latent reentrancy risk if runner ever parallelizes. Safe under serial execution, fails silently if parallelism added. Pattern identified in code-review but not blocking.

Builtin routines judges re-execute runBuiltinRoutine() in judge phase (not querying DB side effects). Each builtin-routine scenario runs the routine twice: once in trigger, once in judge. Double execution cost and judges trigger side effects instead of observing them. Works but violates separation.

Unsafe `as` casts on FireResult (8 instances: lines 383, 399, 404 in builtin-routines.ts; 297, 300, 398, 401 in delegation.ts). When checkAndFireRoutine returns `fired: false`, the `.reason` property is undefined; casts silently produce undefined instead of compile error.

Feature breakdown re-discovers scenarios at report time (runner.ts:334 calls discoverScenarios() again). Scenarios were already loaded and executed; feature should be stored during execution, not re-discovered for reporting. Minor inefficiency but violates DRY principle.

Duplicate dimension ID 'notes_logged' (judges.ts: judgeLogTaskCalled line 184 and judgeNotesLogged line 1039). If both appear in same rubric, scoring engine has duplicate dimension IDs. Currently no scenario uses both, but pattern is brittle.

LLM-as-judge implementations (2 of ~60 dimensions) use heuristic keyword matching in session notes, not true LLM evaluation. Spec §11 promises 'judge's reasoning' but actual dims are fragile regex checks. Either commit to true LLM judging or remove LLM-as-judge label.

Index file (scenarios/index.ts) has feature comments above alphabetically-sorted exports; feature groups don't align with comments. Comments become maintenance debt when scenarios are reordered. Should either group by feature or remove comments entirely.

POC scenario (poc-session-notes.ts) still has inline judge functions duplicating judges.ts factories (sessionCompleted, costTracked, sessionNotesWritten). Should refactor to use reusable factories to prevent divergence when judge logic updates.

AC6 verification bar ambiguous: 'multi-model runs reveal degradation' and 'non-zero scores' are tested, but quality floor undefined. Scenarios could legitimately score 0.1 or 1.0 across models. Future evals need explicit bar (e.g. 'feature average > 0.7') to make cross-model comparison conclusive.
